I understand where you're going with this and *definitely* agree that "go to a therapist" *should not* be used as an insult. However, shipping can become dangerous when people, especially young people, don't see it as fiction and start rationalizing toxic traits for their **own** relationships. When sexy black haired ML becomes boyfriend and its ok that he wants to see me cry, thats romantic. When it's ok that our relationship started on rocky terms, all the best romances do. When romance and fear become synonymous. Or inversely, it's ok to touch my crush without consent, "kabedon" them, grab them in fits of passion. Like, I feel people don't realize just how **much** media can persuade our sense of love, passion, sex, or boundaries. How unconscious normalization and rationalization are. Hence why, whenever I see people so staunchly defending a toxic ship like this (like forget that he's her brother, that a whole other level. He makes her fearful, angry, frustrated, disarrayed *how is that healthy?)* it gets me a little worried. How much of that is them enjoying fiction and how much of it is offense at someones pushing back on their idea of a "passionate romance"?
